findings.evidence: `rg -n "integral_fourierAtom_eq|charFun.*fourierAtom|fourierAtom.*charFun" code/TauCeti/Analysis/Bochner/FourierConvention.lean` finds only the forward theorem at line 61; the roadmap explicitly asks for a conversion between the two conventions at `roadmap/TauCetiRoadmap/OneParameterSemigroups/README.md:218-219`, and downstream Bochner uniqueness needs the arbitrary-`t` direction.
findings.fix: Add the inverse characteristic lemma, e.g. `MeasureTheory.charFun μ t = ∫ q, fourierAtom (((-2 * Real.pi)⁻¹) • t) q ∂μ`, with the appropriate `[simp]`/normal-form annotation if it is intended for rewriting.
findings.issue: Only the forward bridge `∫ q, fourierAtom a q ∂μ = charFun μ ((-2 * Real.pi) • a)` is public; there is no inverse theorem for an arbitrary `t`, so users proving characteristic-function equality/uniqueness from Fourier-convention equality must manually choose `a = (-2 * Real.pi)⁻¹ • t` and redo the nonzero-π scalar proof.

summary: The forward convention bridge is exposed, but the API is missing the inverse rescaling form needed to move arbitrary `charFun μ t` goals back to the Fourier-convention integral without redoing scalar algebra downstream.
